subject: giraffe
pitch: A young reticulated giraffe. Chestnut patches outlined by bright cream lines all over its body and neck, a short mane of stiff brown hair down the neck, two fuzzy ossicones with black tufts on top, big ears, long lashes, a long dark tongue just peeking out, and slender legs fading to cream above the hooves.
reasoning:
I'm planning the giraffe's proportions and skeleton structure, sketching out approximate heights for the hips, shoulders, and head, then setting up the root joint and spine chain positions.

Now I'm defining the full skeletal layout: spine joints running from hips to shoulders, a forward-leaning neck chain of catmull points up to the head, a head joint with jaw, a drooping tail chain with a tuft, and the legs built from hip-to-knee-to-fetlock segments with hoof placement based on target leg length and bend distances.

Working out leg joint names and sweep radii...

For coloring, I'm applying patch-based coat painting to the legs so they fade from patterned near the body to cream near the hooves, using a cream-to-chestnut patch pattern with sized, seeded gaps for natural variation.

Now I'm working on the body geometry, sweeping a radius profile along the spine path between the hips and shoulders to form a deep chest and narrower rump, setting joint positions for the hips and shoulders to anchor the sweep.

Checking leg placement relative to the belly and total height — neck plus head puts the giraffe around 2.9 meters, reasonable for a young giraffe, with a realistic sloping back. Now I'm defining the neck's tapering radius profile and chaining it to the last spine joint to continue the sweep.

Working out the neck path with four names ending in a tip, then placing the head joint at the neck tip with a forward lean so the skull sits naturally atop the spine.

Still working out head geometry...

I'll let it hang from the jaw bone, then pose the jaw open about 6 degrees around the x-axis to reveal the tongue, applying that pose after the jaw parts are built. For the eyes, I'm placing glossy black spheres on either side of the head with small white highlight dots for a bit of life.

Now I'm adding eyelashes as a ring of spikes around each eye, radiating outward along an arc from -80 to 80 degrees so they frame the upper lid, checking that the eye position sits properly within the skull's radius along the head's local axis.

Working out the ears next: using scaled sphere geometry to shape leaf-like ear forms, positioning them on the sides of the head and aiming them outward and slightly upward.

I'll skip the inner ear detail and move on to the ossicones -- adding two rods from the skull top angled up-back, each capped with a small fuzzy black tuft sphere at the tip.

For the mane, I'm thinking stiff brown spikes running along the neck using a sweep function, placing them on the dorsal side where the tube curves upward — figuring out which angle corresponds to the back side given the neck's forward lean and tilted tangent direction.

Still writing spike placement logic...

I'm skipping exact gap tuning for the cream patch lines, settling on a reasonable size rather than worrying about exact scale. Then I'm layering countershading for the belly and neck underside to pale them, and planning a separate head paint with a tan base and darker nose accent.

For the legs, I'm setting up a radius taper along the chain from hip to fetlock with a knee bump, keeping the coat flat-colored via countershade and a gradient blending cream into the leg coat, and considering whether to add a distinct hoof shape at the tip.

I'm adding a hoof as a small cylinder sized to sit flush at ground level below the foot target, then working out leg bone lengths and bend directions for front versus hind legs, keeping front legs mostly straight like a giraffe's.

For the hind legs I'm planning a three-segment chain (hip, stifle, hock, hoof) with alternating forward/backward bends to mimic a natural hock joint, while front legs stay simpler with just two segments bending forward at the knee.

Naming each joint by side (L/R) and front/hind, I'm parenting front legs to the chest joint and hind legs to the hips, checking that leg placement at x≈0.13-0.16 keeps them visible along the body's outer radius without poking through too far.

Now I'm sketching the tail as a drooping catmull-rom chain from the hips down to about y=0.45, tapering the sweep radius and planning a dark tuft of spikes at the tip to finish it off.

Still working out tail geometry...

Actually, maybe I should just set hips joint at -0.4 relative to body start instead of using extend, with a spine chain running from hips through spine2 to chest, making sure hips is created first as the root joint for proper parenting.

I'm defining the spine chain with spine1 colocated with hips, then spine2 and chest following the Catmull curve, and skinning the body sweep to this chain so the rump cap stays owned by spine1. Now I'm working out the radius function along the spine, varying rx and ry with sine curves to taper the body shape.

I'm placing the tail root and checking total height, estimating the neck and head add up to roughly 2.7 units, which feels plausible for a young giraffe with its shorter neck and proportionally larger head compared to an adult.

I decide to shorten the neck slightly, rescaling the neck control points so the head tops out around 2.45-2.5m total height, and set the head joint with a forward-up pitch of about 17 degrees to match typical giraffe posture. Now I'm defining the tapering neck radius values along the chain.

For the head, I'm building the skull as a capsule shape joined to the neck tip, then adding a tapered muzzle capsule extending forward, a dark nose pad sphere at the tip, and tiny nostril spheres, with the head colored a tan shade.

I'm now setting up the lower jaw as a separate bone joined to the head, building its own tapered capsule shape to sit beneath the muzzle, and checking that the gap between the upper muzzle and jaw radii lines up properly at the mouth.

I'm positioning a small tongue capsule emerging from the jaw, angled to peek slightly past the closed lips rather than poke through the muzzle, giving it a rounded tip and a dark purple color.

Then I rotate the jaw open about 8 degrees around its hinge joint, tilting it forward slightly. For the eyes, I'm placing them protruding from the sides of the skull at roughly x=0.085, accounting for the skull's radius there.

Each eyeball is a small dark glossy sphere with a tiny white highlight sphere offset outward and upward to suggest a glint. I'm computing the highlight position by taking the eye socket location and nudging it along the outward direction plus a bit up. I'm skipping brow bumps and eyelid details for now to keep things simple, though I note lashes could be added as a ring around the eye later.

Now I'm setting up lashes as a ring of small black spikes arranged in an arc around the eye, angled outward with a tilt so they lean away from the face, then moving on to position the ears using a direction vector and figuring out how to offset the ear's sphere center along that direction so the shape reads correctly, accounting for scaling and orientation fallback when the direction is mostly sideways.

Working out the orientation math so the thin axis aligns with front-back while the ear length runs along local y, using the up vector to resolve which perpendicular direction becomes the broad face.

For the ossicones, I'm placing the base near the skull top with a slight inward offset, tapering the rod radius toward the tip, and planning to add a fuzzy dark tuft at the end to match giraffe anatomy.

Still working out bone inheritance...

Explicit bone passed to spikes always wins over inherited bone, so I'll set bone: head there since there are no joints to resolve. For the tuft, I'm adding an icosahedron geometry at the tip plus a small ring of black spikes, then defining the brown color palette for chest, cream, belly, and mane.

Now I'm setting up the patches API for cream lines and defining a dark brown mane, then building a hair sweep along the neck using 16-18 spike instances whose direction vectors lean back based on the surface normal at each point.

I'll skip randomized scatter and spots for simplicity, keeping skull shading subtle with a tan countershade, and extend the body coat pattern down onto the legs using a cream gradient fade near the lower limbs.

For the hooves I'll use small six-sided cylinders, and give the tail a chestnut-brown sweep with a black tuft at the end -- skipping extra details like knees, chest definition, mouth lines, and head mane-lets to keep things clean.

Now I'm defining helper vectors for the head's forward and up directions so I can position facial features relative to the head joint, though I need to confirm whether that joint's position is stored as a Vector3 or a plain array before building the positioning helper function.

Writing head anatomy code...

Eye spheres use small radius with few segments; for lashes I'll loop a ring around the eye's axis, treating the eye part's default orientation as outward-facing.

Now building the leg builder, looping over left/right sides with a sign variable and front leg setup...

Writing front limb points...

I need to use the last joint in the joint array instead for the hoof bone, and give the hoof a flat cylinder shape. For the chest, I'll reference spine's tip joint. Now I'm setting up the hind leg with its own root and target points, segment lengths summing slightly longer than the actual distance, and alternating bend directions for a natural knee-hock look.

I'm defining tapering radius arrays for the hind leg and neck, deciding to keep the mane confined to the neck only and skip extra spine hair or belly details to keep things simple. Finalizing the structure to return the body root and move on to writing the actual generation code with hoof coloring.
